summary: The root كمل (kml) primarily means to be or become perfect. It can also mean complete, entire, whole, or full, though the root تمم (tmm) is more precise for these latter meanings.
lane: 1 كَمَلَ ذ He, or it, was, or became, perfect; and sometimes, it was, or became, complete, entire, whole, or full; which latter signification is more properly expressed by تَمَّ , which see.

headwords.def: كَمَلَ He, or it, was, or became, perfect; and sometimes, it was, or became, complete, entire, whole, or full; which latter signification is more properly expressed by تَمَّ, which see.
كَاملٌ Complete with respect to bodily vigour, having attained the usual term thereof. See لَيْثُ عِفِرِّينَ, art. عفر. Also Consummate, perfect.
مُكَمِّلَاتُ Supererogatory acts of religious service.

headword_note: Lane indexes geminate roots with two letters where the Corpus uses three; both spellings are resolved here.
